newsitem.title: UK: Ex-UK Asia air cargo market firm, spot rating seen.
newsitem.headline: Ex-UK Asia air cargo market firm, spot rating seen.

text.p: Air cargo business to the Far East and Australia continues to be generally firm but some spot rating is also reported as the market awaits possible or announced spring cargo rate changes, industry sources told Reuters.

British Airways World Cargo has announced formal rate increases of seven percent from March 17 to Japan, Asia, Australia and India. Some of its competitors have decided on increases while others are still considering their position.
Sterling continued strength does not yet appear to have affected airborne exports to Asia, although most sources now expect this to work through before long.

They added that major West European airlines -- who had earlier announced rate rises -- are now spot rating or discounting on some routes in an effort to hold volumes and this may be drawing business away from the UK.

Rates to Narita are around 1.98 stg per kg average for 100 kgs compared to 1.95 stg on February 6. For 1,000 kgs the current average is 1.30 stg a kg. Average rates to Seoul are broadly similar, market sources said.
"Business is good and we are filling our flights but it is not buzzing at the moment," said Japan Airline Co Ltd UK cargo sales manager, Tony Edwards.

"We're doing OK for February and anticipating a very good March, as Japanese companies step-up imports ahead of the March end to the financial year. The increase in the consumption tax to five from three percent on April 1, is also expected to boost short-term import demand," he added.
However the airline does not intend to apply a spring rate increase and it "will wait and see. If business booms we will put up rates later in the year," Edwards said

JAL is also planning one extra Boeing 747-200 freighter for March 3, possibly one on March 18 and a third "almost certainly" for March 18. Earlier in the month on March 2, there will be a 747-100F flight carrying 40 horses to Tokyo via Anchorage from the UK and Ireland.
The Korean market is however "not as buoyant as it has been," and "overall the airfreight market is not as good as last year," said Korean Air Lines UK cargo manager, Frank Smith.
Another Asian airline executive described the Korean market as "fairly quiet", while a third said "it was pretty good"..

And while KAL is carrying "a bit more cargo to Japan than before", business to Korea itself reflects somewhat weaker domestic demand for luxury products, and an uncertain political and economic situation, he added.
Smith said there was some pressure for rate increases but that he was trying to hold his ground on any rises. And in the meantime, the ex-UK fuel surcharge of six pence a kg remains in force.
Recently introduced Chinese import duties may have also hit Korean manufactured exports, and in turn this has reduced Korean demand for some UK products, he added.
Rates to Seoul are unchanged at an average 1.95 stg a kg for 100 kg and around 1.30 stg kg average for 1,000 kg.

Demand for Hong Kong however remains strong as the market catches up with business after the Chinese New Year break "It is busier than we expected," said James Gilliard from Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd.
The airline has already announced an average ex-UK rates rise of five percent from April 1, while keeping the fuel surcharge.
Average current rates are 1.20 stg a kg for a 100 kgs, against 1.22 stg on February 6, while the 1,000 kg rate is close one stg a kg, market sources said.
Cathay is also seeing good demand for its twice weekly freighter from the UK to Bombay, Gilliard added.

The Australian market was variously described as "fairly quiet" by one source to "very good with the lack of capacity a problem" . Lack of demand on the return leg is seen as a limiting factor in putting on extra outward flights, the sources said.
Rates to Sydney are marginally firmer around 2.18 stg a kg for 100 kg compared to the previous 2.15 stg, while the 1,000 kg is being quoted at an average two stg, they added.
"Although January was better than expected, I'm not sure of the outlook," said Philippine Airlines UK Cargo manager, Keith O'Callaghan and "generally business is quite good for the time of year."

"Business is probably up 100 pct on this time last year while capacity is up by more than a third," he added. The airline recently moved to London-Heathrow from Gatwick and has also introduced non-stop Airbus A340-200 services between the Philippines and the UK.
"Freight to the Philippines is especially buoyant but there is also a good demand to both Japan and Australia," O'Callaghan said.
The airline is eyeing a possible ex-UK cargo rate rise in April or May, but he stressed that market conditions are still being evaluated before a decision is taken.
Average rates to Manila are an average 1.40 stg a kg unchanged on the previous report with a 1,000 kg at 1.15 a kg, industry sources said.
New factories around Subic Bay are also boosting airfreight demand as they require imports which are then transformed into added-value products for exports, the sources added.
"All available space is being used and several freighters could be filled if they were available -- on flights to Jakarta --" said PT Garuda Indonesia cargo executive Nina Sturrock.

Australia is an important onward market from Jakarta with transhipment facilities offered to other Asian destinations including Korea, Beijing and Guangzhou. Over 30 tonnes a week are being moved ex-UK on its two weekly McDonnell Douglas MD-11 flights, which will rise to three a week when the summer schedule starts.
"We're looking at a competitive April 1 rate increase but the exact details are still under discussion," Sturrock added.
Singapore Airlines freight capacity is being well-taken up with flights:"going out pretty full" to most destinations, said UK and Ireland cargo manager Barry Gibson.
The airline has already said it will be upping its ex-UK cargo rates from April 1.

"Overall business is little changed on last year and possibly a bit soft for the time of year," said Malaysian Airline System cargo manager, Shahid Mir, adding that "the Far East market is still getting over the effect of long Chinese New Year break and Hari Raya."
The airline is looking at rate increases on selected routes from April although details still have to finalised, he added.

Demand is also firm to the Middle East though possibly not as strong as some periods of last year. Rates are around 0.82 stg a kg per 100 kg to Dubai and Cairo against, and unchanged to Bahrain at 0.92 stg.

Emirates cargo manager, Ray Disson said that freight levels are very satisfactory, although capacity is not being fully used, "but this reflects that we now have a daily capacity of 70 tonnes -- with our Boeing 777s -- compared to 40 tonnes year ago. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel 44-171-542-7706 Fax +5017
